incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple OOM/container restarts observed in gpu-pool-4 (us-west2). Aggregated alerts: 23 node flaps in last 45m. Opening incident thread for live mitigation. https://internal/incidents/INC-2024-174900

maria: Seeing a cluster of exit code 137s + cuda driver resets. First spike at ~1749001200. Node list: gpu-4-12, gpu-4-14, gpu-4-19 flapped.

sanjay: I pulled /var/log/runtime/serve.log from gpu-4-14, looks like slow growth in "attention_page" allocator. KV cache slab fragmentation slowly creeping, slab_inuse ratio -> 0.86 over 36h. Attached tail: ```
[2024-06-12T02:18:03Z] ERROR runtime: failed to allocate 128MB for attention_page: cudaErrorUnknown: driver shutting down
[2024-06-12T02:18:03Z] INFO runtime: process exiting code=137 pid=17234
[2024-06-12T02:19:12Z] WARN kv: slab_fragmentation=0.72 kv_pages=12345 leased=0
[2024-06-12T02:20:33Z] WARN kv: slab_fragmentation=0.75 kv_pages=12410 leased=0
```

jen: Confirming customer impact: several large customers in us-west2 (acme-inc, betaapps) reported increased 5xxs and timed-out requests to generation endpoints. Incidents page shows spike in 5xx rate from 0.6% -> 4.8% starting 02:15Z. Opening customer-notify draft.

maria: Immediate mitigations enacted: 1) Draining gpu-4-14 from serving pool (kubectl cordon + drain - ignore-daemonsets), 2) toggled emergency eviction policy for KV cache to aggressive, 3) fallback routing of new requests to dedicated fallback-pool in us-west2 (smaller models only).

jen: Commands run: ```
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon gpu-4-14 && kubectl drain gpu-4-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
# set emergency env for runtime on pool (rolling env update)
kubectl set env ds/runtime REDWOOD_KV_EVICT_RATIO=0.12 REDWOOD_KV_EAGER_COMPACT=true -n inference-us-west2
```

liam: Pushed a temporary runtime knob: REDWOOD_PAGED_ATTENTION_COMPACT=true on rollout, this forces slab compaction on free for attention pages. It will increase CPU but should slow fragmentation growth. Monitoring memory headroom now.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: drain started on gpu-4-14 at 1749003150, pod eviction in progress. Fallback routing rule applied to route new sessions to fallback-pool-usw2.

sanjay: Adding diagnostic: capturing jemalloc stats and cuda-meminfo snapshot before restart, please run on drained node if you still have access: ```
curl -sS localhost:6060/debug/jemalloc > /tmp/jemalloc-gpu-4-14.json
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-mem-gpu-4-14.csv
```

maria: Quick customer impact assessment:
- ACME-INC (heavy streaming generation): 12% of requests retried/failed, temporary degraded throughput for large-context jobs.
- BetaApps (low-latency chat): 8% increased latency, some sessions saw aborted streams.
- Several small customers: transient 503s while routing fallback started.

jen: Noted pattern: fragmentation + small steady leak in attention_page leading to occasional cuda allocation failure -> container OOM -> node pod restarts -> k8s reschedules -> sequence repeats when node returns to serving. This is slow-creep failure, not single catastrophic alloc.

liam: Proposed medium-term mitigations for next 24h: 1) enable periodic slab compaction job (cronjob per node), 2) reduce default kv prefix cache TTL from 30m -> 5m for high-activity models, 3) add soft cap to attention_page pool (fail early to fallback model).

sofia: For immediate oncall actions: - keep drained nodes out until we confirm compaction reduces frag by >10% and no OOMs for 30m - monitor OOM rate across cluster (alert if >5 OOMs/15m) - escalate to runtime oncall lead if reoccur >3 times on any single node.

maria: Running compaction check now on gpu-4-19 (still up): ```
curl -sS localhost:6060/debug/kv/compact | jq .summary
{"fragments_before":0.78, "fragments_after":0.61, "freed_bytes":23456789}
```
Looks promising on that node, fragmentation dropped ~17%.

sanjay: Observed one node with PCIe errors in dmesg which might correlate with cuda resets. Logged serial: ```
[ 3428.123456] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 3428.123789] nvidia: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```
We should treat hardware flakiness as potential cofactor; ops to run SMART and firmware checks on these nodes.

ops-bot: :information_source: k8s-bot scheduled restart for runtime daemonset rollout at 1749004800 to pick up REDWOOD_PAGED_ATTENTION_COMPACT env. Rolling restart in 10m window.

jen: Customer comms: Draft to affected customers queued. Short note: "We're investigating intermittent OOMs causing 5xxs in us-west2. We've routed traffic to fallback capacity and are performing emergency memory compaction. We'll update in 30m or sooner." Approving to send.

maria: Handoff note for next oncall (sofia): state=mitigated but not resolved. Actions done: drained gpu-4-14, set aggressive eviction envs, rolled compact knob, started jemalloc + nvidia snapshots, fallback routing active, customer-notify sent.

sofia: Taking over oncall. I'll monitor OOM counts and fragmentation metrics: /dashboards/runtime/paged-attn and /alerts/oom-rate. My escalation criteria: if any node has >2 OOMs in 10m or fragmentation >0.8 persist after compaction.

maria: Leaving runbook pointers: run "kubectl logs -n inference-us-west2 -l runtime=true --tail 200" and look for "cudaError" / "failed to allocate" strings. If trending again, temporarily move high-context models to dedicated pool or reduce max_context_tokens to avoid attention page bloat.

sofia: Acknowledged. I'll keep this thread updated. Next update at +30m or on any new flaps. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status: ACTIVE -> PARTIALLY_MITIGATED. Mitigations applied: node drain, emergency eviction, compaction knob, fallback routing. Severity: P2.

k8s-bot: :white_check_mark: gpu-4-14 successfully drained and cordoned at 1749003300. Pods moved to fallback-pool-usw2.

maria: Leaving final note before sign-off: we've avoided a widespread outage by failing over to smaller models and compaction. Still need postmortem focusing on allocator fragmentation and kernel-level PCIe resets. Please collect node-level firmware/driver versions for affected hosts.

sofia: Signing on. I'll post a 1hr triage summary and open follow-up ticket to schedule hardware checks and an allocator regression/patch if compaction isn't a long-term fix.

jen: :eyes: will also add evals to catch workload that causes attention_page growth (prompt sets + long prefix workloads).

sofia: Handoff complete. Monitoring...
